pr.title: coverage: Extract hole spans from HIR instead of MIR
pr.description:
This makes it possible to treat more kinds of nested item/code as holes, instead of being restricted to closures.

(It also potentially opens up the possibility of using HIR holes to modify branch or MC/DC spans, though we currently don't actually do this.)

Thus, this new implementation treats the following as holes:
- Closures (as before, including `async` and coroutines)
- All nested items
- Inline `const` (because why not)

This gives more accurate coverage reports, because lines occupied by holes don't show the execution count from the enclosing function.

Fixes #126626.

---

[Representative example of the improved coverage instrumentation for functions containing nested items.](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/127199/commits/63c04f05e60ce27311fc1b874907188616beb558#diff-63049890796abe7dade4458e3961d536e3a6a9cd5451df834008cc8b0531825c)
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage originally derived "hole" spans (regions to carve out of an enclosing function's coverage spans) from MIR statements that assign closure-like aggregates. That missed non-closure nested items, so their source lines were reported as executable code of the enclosing function and inherited its execution count, producing misleading coverage (issue #126626). The fix instead extracts hole spans from HIR: a visitor records every nested item span, closure expression span, and inline const block span, filters them to spans directly visible within the function body, and feeds them to the existing hole-sorting/merging/carving stage. MIR no longer contributes holes.
analysis.originalLogic: During extraction of initial coverage spans from MIR, each filtered statement span was inspected with `is_closure_like`: `StatementKind::Assign(box (_, Rvalue::Aggregate(box ref agg_kind, _)))` returning true only for `AggregateKind::Closure(_, _) | AggregateKind::Coroutine(_, _) | AggregateKind::CoroutineClosure(..)`. True meant the span was pushed to `holes`; false meant it was pushed to `initial_covspans`. `extract_covspans_and_holes_from_mir` returned both `covspans` and `holes`, and `extract_refined_covspans` sorted/merged those MIR-derived holes before carving them out of coverage spans. The patch description says: "A statement that looks like the assignment of a closure expression is treated as a \"hole\" span, to be carved out of other spans."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation restricted holes to closure/coroutine aggregates discovered in the enclosing function's MIR. Consequently spans of all other nested items (inner `fn` declarations and bodies, structs, impls/methods, `macro_rules!`, etc.) remained ordinary coverage spans of the enclosing function. Their lines therefore displayed the enclosing function's execution count even though the nested item's body does not execute as part of the enclosing MIR. The description states the old implementation was "restricted to closures", and the removed FIXME said: "When an inner (non-closure) function has `#[coverage(off)]`, its lines can still be marked with misleading execution counts from its enclosing function." The corrected transformation instead treats "Closures (as before, including `async` and coroutines)", "All nested items", and "Inline `const`" as holes using a HIR visitor, then filters with `body_span.contains(hole_span) && body_span.eq_ctxt(hole_span)` and merges/carves those HIR hole spans.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions whose bodies contain nested source constructs: closures (including async blocks/coroutines), nested `fn` items (used or unused, optionally `#[coverage(off)]`/`#[coverage(on)]`), struct definitions, impl blocks with methods, `macro_rules!` definitions, inline `const { ... }` blocks, and async blocks. Spans may come from macro expansion and have differing syntax contexts. The enclosing function may itself be async. Also applicable to doctest/crate-level coverage tests.
analysis.trigger: A function body contains a nested item or other non-closure hole candidate whose span lies within the enclosing body span. Because the old MIR-based detection only recognizes closure/coroutine aggregate assignments, the nested item's span is emitted as an enclosing-function coverage span, so lines inside the nested item show the enclosing function's count (notably when the nested function is `#[coverage(off)]` or never executed).
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and the function is being processed by the InstrumentCoverage pass.
The nested construct's span is directly visible within the enclosing function body span (the fix requires `body_span.contains(hole_span) && body_span.eq_ctxt(hole_span)`).
The nested construct is not a closure/coroutine, since those were already handled by the old MIR `is_closure_like` check.
pitfalls: Deriving holes only from enclosing-function MIR is incomplete: nested item bodies are not part of that MIR, so they cannot be recognized there.

Do not recurse into a nested item after recording its span; the visitor deliberately avoids calling `walk_item` because item children are separate functions/bodies. But nested bodies that are not items must still visit items inside them, hence `NestedFilter = All`.
Filter candidate holes by both containment and syntax context (`body_span.contains(hole_span) && body_span.eq_ctxt(hole_span)`), otherwise unrelated/macro-expanded spans could be carved out.
The `body_span` argument is not always `hir_body.value.span`; the code notes it is "Usually `hir_body.value.span`, but not always" because closure body spans may be unexpanded for async desugaring.

Overlapping or adjacent holes must be merged (`merge_if_overlapping_or_adjacent`) before carving, and holes are separate from coverage spans; removing MIR hole collection must not break signature-span insertion, which now depends only on `!covspans.is_empty()`.
Changing hole spans alters coverage mapping layout and raw bytes in `.cov-map` files even where line-level counts look unchanged; expected outputs must be regenerated/updated.
analysis.testStrategy: Add/extend coverage tests that compare annotated `.coverage` output and `.cov-map` mappings. The new `tests/coverage/holes.rs` covers a closure across multiple lines, an unused nested `fn _unused_fn() {}`, a struct, an impl method, a `macro_rules!`, an inline `const { 7 + 4 }` block, and an async block, with `black_box(())` separates. Expected `holes.coverage` shows nested-item/closure-body lines as non-executable blanks or their own zero counts, while `black_box` lines retain the enclosing count. Update `tests/coverage/async` expectations so lines inside nested `fn c`/`fn d` are no longer marked executed and remove the explanatory comment; remove the #126626 FIXMEs from `tests/coverage/attr/nested.rs` and `off-on-sandwich.rs` and expect nested `#[coverage(off)]` function lines to be blank; update `no_cov_crate.coverage` so `inner_not_covered` lines are blank; update doctest/closure_macro/cov-map expectations. Construct a two-variant differential pair with identical source except one wraps an inner item in `#[coverage(off)]`/makes it unused: the old behavior reports enclosing counts on its lines, the fixed behavior reports blank/zero.
